evidence: Supplied manual API forms and authored offline tests; no native file comparison or printing

sources.topic: COMPARE_FILE names, open writable result FILE, ASCII differing lines and binary first-difference example
PRINT_FILE ASCII input, default output and unsupported nowait note

implemented.backends: Bounded detached closed-file reads from MemoryFiles or explicitly rooted DirectoryFiles; fresh disk bytes and no read-cache mutation
implemented.comparison: Same-numbered ASCII records with CR/LF/CRLF normalization or one-based binary first unequal byte/EOF; zero when equal
implemented.report: Compact ASCII JSON summary and per-record differences; one write after full validation, capacity and budget checks; normal FILE cursor, append and ATR_EOL semantics
implemented.printing: Entire ASCII input validated before <=254-character WRITE recorder/callback chunks, preserving original newlines; synchronous for both nowait values
implemented.ownership: Disjoint checked outputs, shared handle identity, protected FOR counters, source capture order, sticky abort and routine output-effect propagation

portable_choices: ASCII comparison does not align lines; final terminator presence is ignored and a blank record differs from no record
Binary diff_count is a one-based first difference including prefix EOF, not a byte mismatch count; this base is not a native encoding claim
Report schema and ASCII escaping are package conventions, independent of proprietary controller report formats
Portable status 0 success, 1 missing input and 3 busy input; failure statuses preserve count/report; validation exceptions preserve pending outputs
Comparison results must use the input backend; no implicit cross-backend or operating-system file lookup
Print callbacks use ordinary output observations; completed earlier effects survive later failure and no callback retry occurs
One execution step per ASCII record, 4096-byte binary block or print chunk; no internal handler scan, cooperative yield or wall-time callback bound
remaining: Native report layout, line alignment, binary offsets/statuses, printer/device discovery, asynchronous spooling, physical PATH node byte layout, strict mode and native acceptance
